item.title: MJR Morning Brief — October 21, 2026
item.description:
From Media Jobs Report, here's your MJR Morning Brief.
FEMA is preparing broadcasters for the nationwide Emergency Alert System test scheduled for November 17 at 2:20 p.m. Eastern.
The one-minute test will reach radio and television stations through FEMA's internet-based alert system, with traditional broadcast monitoring providing backup. Stations should verify equipment connectivity, audio quality, and automatic retransmission settings before test day. Broadcasters must also submit their FCC EAS reporting Form One by October 30.
In television news,
CBS has revealed the first performers for its New Year's Eve Live: Nashville's Big Bash. HARDY, Little Big Town and ACM Award-winning group The Red Clay Strays will take the stage for the nearly five-hour celebration on December 31. The special airs on CBS and streams on Paramount Plus, with additional performers to be announced. Fans can also attend the free downtown Nashville celebration featuring the traditional midnight Music Note Drop.
Turning to radio,
Cumulus Media has launched a new local morning show on Indianapolis station 107.9 The Mix. The Morning Mix with Toni and Ryan pairs Toni DeKeyser and Ryan Swiger weekdays from six to ten. The launch also reshuffles midday programming between The Mix and sister station 99.5 ZPL, while Swiger continues afternoon drive on ZPL.
On the education front,
Investigative Reporters and Editors has named three journalists to its 2027 Chauncey Bailey Fellowship. Daisy Zavala Magaña, Miguel Torres and Nushrat Rahman will investigate farmworker pesticide exposure, immigration-service fraud and rental housing conditions. The yearlong program provides training and mentorship while honoring the legacy of Oakland investigative journalist Chauncey Bailey.
Turning to technology,
nextKast has released version 7.1.4 of its radio automation software, adding new tools to improve commercial scheduling and station operations. The update introduces nextTraffic Audit, allowing broadcasters to verify that all advertising spots are scheduled and quickly correct incomplete logs. Other improvements include enhanced traffic scheduling, format monitoring and fixes for live playout operations. The update is available now from nextKast.
In radio news,
Gordon Deal’s This Morning, America’s First News is expanding its reach, adding 20 new affiliates, including KMOX in St. Louis, WCCO in Minneapolis, and KMBX in Las Vegas. The Compass Media Networks program now airs on more than 325 stations, reaching 91 of the nation’s top 100 radio markets. Deal says the growth is both humbling and motivating.
On the education front,
The University of Washington has opened a new four-control-room broadcast production facility powered by Grass Valley technology. Called Sundodger Studios, the IP-based center can handle multiple live sporting events simultaneously, while giving students hands-on experience with professional cameras, production switchers and broadcast workflows.
In media education news,
The New York Times is accepting applications for its 2027-28 journalism fellowship. The paid, yearlong program offers early-career journalists opportunities in reporting, video, visuals, data journalism and audience engagement. Applicants must have fewer than five years of professional journalism experience. The fellowship begins June seventh, 2027, and applications close November twentieth.
And finally,
KROQ in Los Angeles has announced the lineup for its 35th Almost Acoustic Christmas concert, December 12 at the Kia Forum. Foo Fighters, Weezer, Sublime and Interpol headline the event, alongside four additional acts. Tickets go on sale October 30, with proceeds benefiting two Los Angeles youth organizations.
For the latest media news, job openings, free tools and more, visit MediaJobsReport.com.
